title: Grade 5 Science — Tue, Jun 17
description: Respiratory System — Day 2 of 5: Organs of the respiratory system
subject: science

questions.question: The correct pathway of air from outside to lungs is:
options: Nose → Pharynx → Larynx → Trachea → Bronchi → Lungs
questions.explanation: Air pathway: Nose/Mouth → Pharynx (throat) → Larynx (voice box) → Trachea (windpipe) → Bronchi → Bronchioles → Alveoli (in lungs).

questions.question: The trachea is:
options: The windpipe — a tube that carries air from the throat to the lungs
questions.explanation: The trachea (windpipe) is a tube, about 11–12 cm long, that carries air from the larynx to the bronchi. C-shaped rings of cartilage keep it open.

questions.question: The trachea splits into two tubes called:
questions.explanation: The trachea divides into two bronchi — one going to the left lung, one to the right lung.

questions.question: Bronchi divide further into smaller tubes called:
questions.explanation: Bronchi branch into smaller bronchioles (smaller tubes within the lungs). Bronchioles further lead to alveoli.

questions.question: Alveoli are:
options: Tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange occurs
The tubes leading to the lungs
questions.explanation: Alveoli (singular: alveolus) are tiny balloon-like air sacs at the end of bronchioles. Oxygen and CO₂ are exchanged here between air and blood.

questions.question: The human lungs have approximately how many alveoli?
questions.explanation: Each lung has about 350 million alveoli — roughly 700 million total. Their combined surface area equals about half a tennis court!

questions.question: Why do alveoli have such a large surface area?
options: To allow maximum gas exchange between air and blood
questions.explanation: Large surface area + thin walls + rich blood supply = fast, efficient gas exchange. More surface area = more oxygen can be absorbed per breath.

questions.question: The diaphragm is:
options: A dome-shaped muscle beneath the lungs that controls breathing
questions.explanation: The diaphragm is a large dome-shaped muscle at the base of the chest. When it contracts (flattens), it pulls air into the lungs. When it relaxes, air is pushed out.

questions.question: The larynx is:
options: The voice box — contains vocal cords that produce sound
questions.explanation: The larynx (voice box) contains the vocal cords. When air passes over them, they vibrate to produce sound/speech.

questions.question: The pharynx is:
options: The throat — the common passageway for both food and air
questions.explanation: The pharynx (throat) is where the digestive and respiratory pathways cross. Food goes to the oesophagus; air goes to the larynx/trachea.

questions.question: The epiglottis is a flap in the throat that:
options: Closes over the trachea when you swallow so food doesn't enter the airway
questions.explanation: The epiglottis covers the entrance to the trachea when swallowing, preventing food from entering the airway. When it fails, we choke.

questions.question: Which is the correct comparison of left and right lungs?
options: Both lungs are exactly the same size
Right lung: 3 lobes, larger. Left lung: 2 lobes, smaller (space for the heart)
Left lung: 3 lobes. Right lung: 2 lobes
questions.explanation: The right lung has 3 lobes and is larger. The left lung has 2 lobes — it is slightly smaller to make space for the heart.

questions.question: The pleura is:
options: A thin double membrane surrounding each lung that protects and reduces friction
A blood vessel in the lungs
questions.explanation: The pleura is a two-layered membrane surrounding the lungs. The fluid between the layers reduces friction as the lungs expand and contract during breathing.

questions.question: The intercostal muscles are:
options: Muscles between the ribs that help expand and contract the chest during breathing
questions.explanation: Intercostal muscles (between the ribs) work together with the diaphragm to change the volume of the chest cavity during breathing.

questions.question: In order, label the air passage: 'Nose → ___ → Larynx → Trachea → ___ → Bronchioles → ___'
questions.explanation: Full pathway: Nose → Pharynx → Larynx → Trachea → Bronchi → Bronchioles → Alveoli.
